notes: Real-world regression from the 'Mangrove test 2' sketch (report 180): two disjoint fragments whose 0.5 km buffers overlap. The small fragment's buffered bbox is fully contained in the large fragment's bbox, so the old estimate (hardMax x lambda) degenerated to hardMax (0.726 km2, 13.7% of naive) and warned, while the true double-counted habitat in buffer(A) intersect buffer(B) is only ~0.376 km2 (7.1% of naive, below the 10% warning gate). Ground truth verified via habitat counts on union/intersection of the buffered geometries against the same raster.
